note: Research discovery queue. Entries are unreviewed leads until an Evidence Decision records a source review. Metadata and screening notes must not be treated as publishable evidence.

candidates.title: Beyond positive thinking: A randomized trial of mental contrasting with implementation intentions to curb academic procrastination
candidates.review_notes: High-priority lead for reviewing WOOP/MCII and task-initiation content. The reported randomized study is small and limited to undergraduates at one private Chinese university, so it must not justify broad population claims or a universal anti-procrastination protocol.

candidates.title: The association between sleep variability and cognitive function: A systematic review and meta analysis
candidates.review_notes: Potential support for treating sleep regularity/variability as a review dimension rather than focusing only on duration. Association evidence must not be converted into a causal prescription without checking study designs, populations, effect sizes and limitations.

candidates.title: Should we all just take 10? A meta-analysis of wakeful rest
candidates.review_notes: Candidate for a post-learning quiet-rest experiment. The meta-analysis reports substantial heterogeneity and weaker effects in healthy younger adults, so Brali must not turn the paper title into a universal ten-minute rule.

candidates.title: Research on the testing effect routinely conflates direct and forward testing effects: A meta-analysis of testing effects with free recall
candidates.container_title: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition
candidates.review_notes: Challenge-existing lead. Brali retrieval-practice claims should distinguish memory for tested material from forward effects on subsequently learned material instead of using one undifferentiated testing-effect claim.

candidates.title: Mixed effects of retrieval practice on the acquisition of procedural knowledge in verb spelling education
candidates.review_notes: Challenge-existing lead for procedural-learning claims. In this classroom study, adding retrieval practice improved long-term rule retention but did not produce superior rule application, so remembering and applying should remain separate outcomes in Brali.

candidates.title: Acute cognitive effects of interruptions to prolonged sitting with brief standing or physical activity breaks: a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis
candidates.container_title: International Journal of Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity
candidates.review_notes: Candidate for reviewing movement-break guidance. The meta-analysis reports small acute executive/memory effects but low or very-low certainty for most outcomes and explicitly says protocol-parameter findings are not sufficient for definitive prescriptions.
